fix(llm): retry with doubled max_tokens when reasoning models hit length limit (#29)

* fix(llm): retry with doubled max_tokens when reasoning models hit length limit

Reasoning models such as deepseek-v4-flash (the new deepseek-chat) and
deepseek-reasoner share the max_tokens budget between reasoning_content
and content. When the thinking phase exhausts the budget before the
answer is produced, the provider returns finish_reason=length with an
empty content field, which StaffDeck treated as an empty response and
retried with the same fixed budget -- guaranteeing failure across all
EMPTY_RESPONSE_RETRIES attempts.

Track a mutable current_max_tokens per call. On each retry, if the
previous attempt was truncated by length AND produced reasoning output,
double the budget (capped at 32768) so the model has room to finish
reasoning and emit content. Applied symmetrically to generate_text
(non-stream) and generate_text_stream.

Verified end-to-end with deepseek-v4-flash: a greeting turn and a SOP
turn (seal_application_approval -> evaluate_compliance) both return
fluent content after the budget escalation.

* fix(llm): preserve token budget above escalation ceiling + add regression tests

Address review feedback on #29: when a model configuration already
requests max_output_tokens above the 32768 escalation ceiling, the
previous min(current*2, 32768) shrunk the retry budget instead of
preserving or increasing it (e.g. [65536, 32768, 32768]).

Extract REASONING_TOKEN_ESCALATION_CEILING and _escalate_reasoning_token_budget()
helper: double the budget up to the ceiling, but keep the configured value
unchanged once it is at or above the ceiling. Applied to both
generate_text and generate_text_stream.

Add four regression tests covering the matrix:
- generate_text: normal escalation (4096 -> 8192)
- generate_text: budget above ceiling preserved (65536 -> 65536)
- generate_text_stream: normal escalation (4096 -> 8192)
- generate_text_stream: budget above ceiling preserved (65536 -> 65536)

fix(scripts): stop native stderr from aborting dev.ps1 on Windows (#57)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop" turns any stderr output from a native command
into a terminating NativeCommandError under Windows PowerShell 5.1, which
broke dev_up.ps1 in two places:

- The interpreter probe: `py -3.11` writes "No suitable Python runtime found"
  to stderr on hosts without 3.11, aborting the loop before the `py -3` and
  `python` candidates were tried. Setup then failed with "Python 3.11 or newer
  is required" even though a newer interpreter was installed.
- The dev.py invocation: vite build warnings relayed on stderr aborted startup
  partway through, leaving no services running and a bare exit code 1.

Switch to exit-code checks for the native calls and silence the probe with
`2>&1 | Out-Null`. `throw` still terminates regardless of the preference, and
`exit $LASTEXITCODE` keeps propagating real failures.

Verified on Windows PowerShell 5.1 with Python 3.12.10 and no 3.11 present:
dev_up.ps1 --detach, dev_status.ps1 and dev_down.ps1 all exit 0 and the app
serves /api/health without a PYTHON override.

* fix(channels): clean up mounts when deleting an employee

Deleting an agent left orphan rows in channel_binding_agents, so the
Feishu/DingTalk /员工 command listed a bare agent_id for a deleted
employee and /切换 could route a conversation to it. delete_agent now
removes the agent's channel mounts, promotes the first remaining mount
to default (syncing binding.agent_id) when the default mount is deleted.
mounted_agents additionally filters mounts whose agent no longer exists,
so legacy orphan rows self-heal across listing, switching, autorouting,
and the channels page; conversation pointers keep resetting through the
existing resolve_current_agent fallback.

needs: three contact-reading scopes (contact:contact.base:readonly,
contact:user.base:readonly, contact:user.id:readonly), the group
message scopes (group_at_msg, group_at_msg.include_bot, group_msg,
group_msg.include_bot:read, im:message:readonly) alongside the existing
p2p/send/reaction scopes. Directory and sensitive group-read entries
move out of the "usually removable" list since they are now required,
and the tooltip copy plus English translations follow suit.

count skill_started/skill_resumed agent events, which only the removed
legacy agent loop used to emit. Harness v2 now records the events when
an SOP task frame is activated — start_new_task emits skill_started,
switch_to_pending emits skill_resumed, continuing the active SOP stays
uncounted — with the legacy payload shape so the stats reader, trace
consumers, and Feishu traces keep working.

Also fix a fallout from the mount cleanup: adopt_orphan_channel_sessions
must claim sessions using raw mount rows instead of the user-facing
filtered mount set, since historical sessions can belong to deleted
employees and still need to migrate to the new binding.
